name: Everest Expedition via the South Col
sub_region: Solukhumbu District, Koshi Province; Sagarmatha National Park; Khumbu Pasang Lhamu Rural Municipality

difficulty.notes: Extreme-altitude expedition on fixed ropes: Khumbu Icefall (ladders, serac hazard), Western Cwm, Lhotse Face (approx. 40-degree ice), Yellow Band, Geneva Spur, South Col, Southeast Ridge, South Summit and Hillary Step. Supplemental oxygen normally used above Camp 2/3. Prior 8,000 m or high 7,000 m experience is typically expected by operators.

duration_days.notes: Standard full expeditions run approx. 55-60 days, including approx. 30-40 days of acclimatization/rotations. Shorter 38-45 day formats rely on pre-acclimatization (hypoxic tents) or rapid formats. The Nepal permit validity has reportedly been shortened (75 to 55 days, UNVERIFIED).

max_altitude_point: Summit of Mount Everest (8,848.86 m, 2020 Nepal-China survey)
start_point: Lukla (flight from Kathmandu, or from Ramechhap/Manthali in peak season)

itinerary.route: Arrive Kathmandu; expedition briefing at the Department of Tourism, permit collection, gear check
Fly to Lukla (from Kathmandu or Manthali/Ramechhap in peak season) and trek Phakding - Namche Bazaar (rest) - Tengboche/Deboche - Dingboche (rest) - Lobuche - Gorak Shep - Everest Base Camp
itinerary.notes: Approach trek with acclimatization days at Namche (3,440 m) and Dingboche (4,360 m); last teahouse night at Lobuche (4,940 m) or Gorak Shep (5,164 m).

itinerary.route: Arrive Everest Base Camp; puja ceremony; ladder, fixed-rope and oxygen training
itinerary.notes: Many teams also climb Lobuche East (6,119 m) as an acclimatization rotation.

itinerary.route: Acclimatization rotations: BC - Khumbu Icefall - Camp 1 (approx. 6,065 m) - Western Cwm - Camp 2 (approx. 6,400 m) - touch/sleep Camp 3 (approx. 7,160 m) on Lhotse Face - return to BC
itinerary.notes: Climb-high, sleep-low; usually two rotations (or one rotation plus Lobuche East).

itinerary.route: Rest at Base Camp (some teams descend to lower villages) awaiting summit weather window
Summit push (weather window, typically mid-late May): BC - Camp 2 - Camp 3 (oxygen) - Camp 4 / South Col (approx. 7,925-7,950 m) - summit 8,848.86 m - descend to South Col/Camp 2 - Base Camp
itinerary.walking_hours: Summit day approx. 10-16 hrs round trip
itinerary.notes: Contingency days for weather are built into this window.

itinerary.route: Clear Base Camp (garbage checks by SPCC); trek down to Lukla
Fly Lukla - Kathmandu (or Manthali); summit certificate formalities at DoT; departure

best_seasons.notes: Nearly all commercial summits are in the spring (March-May permit season; summit windows usually mid-late May). Autumn and winter Everest ascents are rare. DoT seasons: spring Mar-May, summer Jun-Aug, autumn Sep-Nov, winter Dec-Feb. Spring 2026 set records: 495 Everest permits and 274 summits in a single day (20 May 2026).

permits.name: Everest royalty, normal (South Col) route, foreign climber - spring (Mar-May)
Everest royalty, normal route, foreign climber - autumn (Sep-Nov)
Everest royalty, normal route, foreign climber - winter (Dec-Feb) and summer/monsoon (Jun-Aug)
Everest royalty, other routes, foreign climber
permits.fee: USD 10,000 spring / USD 5,000 autumn / USD 2,500 winter-summer per person

permits.name: Everest royalty, Nepali climbers, normal route
permits.fee: NPR 150,000 spring / NPR 75,000 autumn / NPR 37,500 winter-summer
permits.applies_to: Nepali citizens (Nepali mountain guides assisting climbers are exempt)

permits.name: Garbage management deposit (Schedule 9, Mountaineering Regulations)
permits.fee: USD 4,000 (refundable) for Mount Everest, deposited by the expedition team

permits.name: Khumbu Icefall route fee (Sagarmatha Pollution Control Committee)
permits.fee: USD 600 per foreign climber (Everest, Lhotse, Nuptse permit holders); late fee if not deposited by end of April 2026

permits.name: Sagarmatha National Park entry
permits.fee: NPR 3,000 per person per entry (SAARC NPR 1,500)

permits.name: Khumbu Pasang Lhamu Rural Municipality entry fee
permits.fee: NPR 3,000 per person (raised from NPR 2,000 per operators)

guide_requirements: Sixth Amendment to the Mountaineering Regulations (gazetted 3-4 Feb 2025; royalty rates effective 1 Sept 2025): solo expeditions on 8,000 m peaks banned; at least one mountain guide or high-altitude worker per two climbers on Everest and other 8,000ers. A government liaison officer must be attached to each expedition under the Tourism Act (daily allowance raised to NPR 1,600 under the 2025 amendment, paid by the team). Mandatory insurance minimums: NPR 2 million for mountain guides/high-altitude workers, NPR 1.5 million for liaison officers and base camp workers. Since 2024, climbers must carry a search-and-rescue device (RECCO-type reflector accepted).

flights: Kathmandu - Lukla, or Manthali (Ramechhap) - Lukla during peak windows (approx. mid-March to mid-May and late September to end November per CAAN practice); Manthali is approx. 4-5 hrs by road from Kathmandu
Helicopter options Lukla/Base Camp area for return
drives: Kathmandu - Manthali (Ramechhap) airport for peak-season Lukla flights
logistics.notes: Teahouses/lodges on the approach; full-service expedition base camp (dining, communications, medical) and tented high camps. 2026 SPCC rules: each climber must bring down at least 8 kg of waste from above base camp, including 2 kg from above Camp 2 (checked at Camp 2); only SPCC/municipality-issued poop bags above base camp (personal bags not accepted); source segregation in 7 categories; inventory of food/equipment above BC at start and end of season; Garbage Clearance Letter withheld from non-compliant teams.

highlights: Summit of the world's highest mountain, 8,848.86 m
Khumbu Icefall, Western Cwm and Lhotse Face
South Col, South Summit and Hillary Step
Sherpa culture of the Khumbu and Tengboche monastery
Classic approach trek through Sagarmatha National Park (UNESCO World Heritage Site)
risks: Khumbu Icefall serac collapse and avalanche
Extreme altitude: HAPE, HACE, hypoxia; oxygen system failure
Crowding/queues on summit days (record 274 summits on 20 May 2026)
Frostbite, extreme cold and jet-stream winds

acclimatization.notes: Rotations between Base Camp and Camps 1-3 over approx. 3-4 weeks before the summit push.

unverified: Garbage deposit: DoT Schedule 9 lists USD 4,000 for Everest per expedition team, while BBC/Kathmandu media describe it as per climber. The government announced (2025-2026) it will scrap the refundable deposit in favour of a non-refundable clean-up fee (expected approx. USD 4,000 per climber), but this depends on the Integrated Tourism Bill and was not in force as of mid-2026.
Khumbu Icefall fee USD 600 per climber for 2026 comes from a single trade-news report of the SPCC notice.
Khumbu Pasang Lhamu municipality fee NPR 3,000 is from operator sources only.
Permit validity reportedly reduced from 75 to 55 days (operator blog only).

Proposed rule requiring proof of a prior summit above 7,000 m in Nepal before an Everest permit: in the Integrated Tourism Bill (passed by the National Assembly Feb 2026; 263 amendments under House committee review July 2026, some proposing 7,000 m + 8,000 m prerequisites, mandatory medical certificates and climber caps). NOT law as of October 2026; operators expect it from 2028 at the earliest.

GPS trackers: no universal personal GPS-tracker mandate is established; the 2024 DoT rule requires a 'tracking chip'/search-and-rescue device, which in practice is a passive RECCO reflector. Drones and GPS-based tracking are proposed in the Clean Mountain Strategy (2025-2029).
